cards.text: Jesus is talking with the Pharisees, a group of strict Jewish religious leaders. They ask Him a big one: when is the kingdom of God going to come? They want a date, friend. They want a tracking number.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Pharisees the kingdom of God will come with observable signs.

cards.text: No signs to watch for. And nobody's going to say, 'Look, here it is,' or 'There it is,' like it's a set of car keys somebody finally found in the couch.

cards.question: So where does Jesus tell the Pharisees the kingdom of God is?

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to His disciples. He calls Himself the Son of Man (Luke 22:48), and He tells them a time is coming when they'll long to see one of the days of the Son of Man.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples that when they long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, they will see it.

cards.text: And people will start shouting, 'Look, there He is!' or 'Look, here He is!' Friend, that's the group chat at 2 a.m. FORTY messages. ZERO facts.

cards.question: When people shout "Look, there He is!" what does Jesus tell the disciples to do?

answers.text: Send one of them to look

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples not to chase those reports. What does He say the Son of Man will be like in His day?

answers.text: Like a quiet knock at night

cards.text: Lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other. Nobody needs a group chat to tell them about THAT.

cards.question: But first, Jesus says, the Son of Man must suffer many things and be ___ by this generation.

cards.text: Suffer many things. Be rejected. Before the lightning comes the hard road, and Jesus doesn't sugarcoat it one bit.
Then Jesus reaches way back to Noah, the man God told to build the ark (Genesis 6:14). He says just as it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the Son of Man.

cards.question: In Noah's day, right up until Noah entered the ark, what were people doing?

cards.text: Then the flood came and destroyed them all. Jesus says it was the same in the days of Lot, Abraham's nephew (Genesis 12:5).

cards.question: Jesus says people in Lot's day were busy buying and selling, planting and building.
Then Lot leaves Sodom. What rains down from heaven that very day?

cards.text: Fire and sulfur, and it destroyed them all. Jesus says it will be just like that on the day the Son of Man is revealed.

cards.question: On that day, Jesus says someone up on the housetop should come down and grab his possessions first.
What does Jesus tell the person out in the field to do on that day?

cards.text: No running back for one more thing. When my drawer opened, I left with nothing but my mustache, and friend, I have NOT missed those takeout menus.
Then Jesus says three words: 'Remember Lot's wife!'

cards.question: Jesus says to remember Lot's wife. Back in Genesis, as she was leaving Sodom, what did she do?

cards.text: She looked back, and she became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26). Her feet were leaving, but I think her heart was still in Sodom.

cards.question: Jesus says whoever tries to save his life will ___ it, but whoever loses his life will ___ it.

cards.text: On that night, Jesus says, two people will be in one bed. Same blanket, same fight over who's hogging it.

cards.question: Two people in one bed on that night: one will be ___ and the other left.
Jesus says two women grinding grain together will both be taken.
After all this, the disciples have a question for Jesus. What do they ask?

cards.text: Jesus answers, 'Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.' That's where He leaves it, friend, and so will I.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'Jesus is talking with the Pharisees...', 'They ask Him a big one...', 'They want a date, friend.' and 'They want a tracking number.' The limit is 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'No signs to watch for.', which comes from Luke 17:20, but it cites only Luke 17:21. The citation should be Luke 17:20-21.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question asks where the kingdom is. 'Far off in the future' is a time, not a place, so it isn't the same kind of answer as 'In their midst' and 'Up in the temple'. It is also arguable within this passage, because verses 22-30 speak of future days of the Son of Man. A baker could defend it.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card says people will 'start shouting'. Luke 17:23 says 'People will tell you'. Shouting stretches the text and doesn't call the action what the text calls it.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke 'FORTY messages. ZERO facts.' tells the baker the reports are false right before card 8 asks what to do about them. That rules out 'Go check it out together' and 'Send one of them to look' and gives away the answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question says 'When people shout'. Luke 17:23 says 'People will tell you'.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This card only restates the answer to card 11 ('Suffer many things. Be rejected.') and adds a comment. It tells nothing new from the passage, so it is a recap card that doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: 'No running back for one more thing' restates the answers to cards 7 and 8. The rest of the card is the drawer joke. The card tells no new part of the passage, so it is a recap card carrying a joke.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: 'I think her heart was still in Sodom' gives a reason why Lot's wife looked back. Genesis 19:26 doesn't give one. Marking it with 'I think' is allowed for feelings, but the Reasons rule does not allow made-up motives.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The card tells Genesis 19:26 (she looked back and became a pillar of salt) and nothing from Luke 17:32, which card 10 already told. Yet it cites Luke 17:32.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This choice card tests a verse outside the passage (Genesis 19:26, Lot's wife looking back) and cites it as its right answer. The docs allow outside facts 'when they help', but they don't say whether a choice card can ask about an outside verse instead of the passage.
findings.question: Can a choice card ask about a verse outside the passage, like Genesis 19:26 for 'Remember Lot's wife!' (Luke 17:32)? Or should outside context only ever be told on story cards?
